exercises.heading: Section 4.5 Exercises
exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, use the information provided to solve the problem.

problem.paragraph: Let $$w\left( {x,y,z} \right) = xy \cos z,$$ where $$x = t,y = t^{2},$$ and $$z = \arcsin t.$$ Find $$\frac{dw}{dt}.$$
Let $$w\left( {t,v} \right) = e^{tv}$$ where $$t = r + s$$ and $$v = rs.$$ Find $$\frac{\partial w}{\partial r}$$ and $$\frac{\partial w}{\partial s}.$$
If $$w = 5x^{2} + 2y^{2},x = -3s + t,$$ and $$y = s - 4t,$$ find $$\frac{\partial w}{\partial s}$$ and $$\frac{\partial w}{\partial t}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\partial w\partial s=94s-46t,\partial w\partial s=94s-46t,$$ $$\partial w\partial t=-46s+74t\partial w\partial t=-46s+74t$$

problem.paragraph: If $$w = xy^{2},x = 5 \cos (2t),$$ and $$y = 5 \sin (2t),$$ find $$\frac{dw}{dt}.$$
If $$f(x,y) = xy,x = r \cos \theta,$$ and $$y = r \sin \theta,$$ find $$\frac{\partial f}{\partial r}$$ and express the answer in terms of $$r$$ and $$\theta.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\partial f \partial r = r sin ( 2 \theta ) \partial f \partial r = r sin ( 2 \theta )$$

problem.paragraph: Suppose $$f(x,y) = x + y,$$ where $$x = r \cos \theta$$ and $$y = r \sin \theta.$$ Find $$\frac{\partial f}{\partial\theta}.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find $$\frac{df}{dt}$$ using the chain rule and direct substitution.

solution.paragraph: $$d f d t = 2 t + 4 t 3 d f d t = 2 t + 4 t 3$$

problem.paragraph: $$f\left( {x,y} \right) = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}},y = t^{2},x = t$$
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = xy,x = 1 - \sqrt{t},y = 1 + \sqrt{t}$$

solution.paragraph: $$d f d t = -1 d f d t = -1$$

problem.paragraph: $$f\left( {x,y} \right) = \frac{x}{y},x = e^{t},y = 2e^{t}$$
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = \ln \left( {x + y} \right),$$ $$x = e^{t},y = e^{t}$$

solution.paragraph: $$d f d t = 1 d f d t = 1$$

problem.paragraph: $$f\left( {x,y} \right) = x^{4},$$ $$x = t,y = t$$

Let $$w\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2},$$ $$x = \cos t,y = \sin t,$$ and $$z = e^{t}.$$ Express $$w$$ as a function of $$t$$ and find $$\frac{dw}{dt}$$ directly. Then, find $$\frac{dw}{dt}$$ using the chain rule.

solution.paragraph: $$dwdt=2e2tdwdt=2e2t$$ in both cases

problem.paragraph: Let $$z = x^{2}y,$$ where $$x = t^{2}$$ and $$y = t^{3}.$$ Find $$\frac{dz}{dt}.$$
Let $$u = e^{x}\sin y,$$ where $$x = \text{-ln} 2t$$ and $$y = \pi t.$$ Find $$\frac{du}{dt}$$ when $$x = \ln 2$$ and $$y = \frac{\pi}{4}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$d u d t = 2 ( \pi -4 ) d u d t = 2 ( \pi -4 )$$

solution.paragraph: $$z=3+y3,z=3+y3,$$ a curve in the $$zy-planezy-plane$$ with rulings parallel to the $$x-axisx-axis$$

problem.paragraph: $$\sin \left( {x + y} \right) + \cos \left( {x - y} \right) = 4$$

solution.paragraph: $$d y d x = y - x - x + 2 y 3 d y d x = y - x - x + 2 y 3$$
$$d y d x = - y x 3 d y d x = - y x 3$$

problem.paragraph: $$x \cos (xy) + y \cos x = 2$$

solution.paragraph: $$d y d x = - y e x y x e x y + e y ( 1 + y ) d y d x = - y e x y x e x y + e y ( 1 + y )$$

problem.paragraph: Find $$\frac{dz}{dt}$$ using the chain rule where $$z = 3x^{2}y^{3},x = t^{4},$$ and $$y = t^{2}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$d z d t = 42 t 13 d z d t = 42 t 13$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$z = 3 \cos x - \sin (xy),x = \frac{1}{t},$$ and $$y = 3t.$$ Find $$\frac{dz}{dt}.$$
Let $$z = e^{1 - xy},x = t^{1/3},$$ and $$y = t^{3}.$$ Find $$\frac{dz}{dt}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$d z d t = - 10 3 t 7 / 3 \times e 1 - t 10 / 3 d z d t = - 10 3 t 7 / 3 \times e 1 - t 10 / 3$$

problem.paragraph: Find $$\frac{dz}{dt}$$ by the chain rule where $$z = \cosh^{2}(xy),x = \frac{1}{2}t,$$ and $$y = e^{t}.$$
Let $$z = \frac{x}{y},x = 2 \cos u,$$ and $$y = 3 \sin v.$$ Find $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial u}$$ and $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial v}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\partial z\partial u=-2sinu3sinv\partial z\partial u=-2sinu3sinv$$ and $$\partial z\partial v=-2cosucosv3sin2v\partial z\partial v=-2cosucosv3sin2v$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$z = e^{x^{2}y},$$ where $$x = \sqrt{uv}$$ and $$y = \frac{1}{v}.$$ Find $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial u}$$ and $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial v}.$$
If $$z = xye^{x/y},$$ $$x = r \cos \theta,$$ and $$y = r \sin \theta,$$ find $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial r}$$ and $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial\theta}$$ when $$r = 2$$ and $$\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\partial z\partial r=3e3,\partial z\partial r=3e3,$$ $$\partial z\partial \theta =(2-43)e3\partial z\partial \theta =(2-43)e3$$

problem.paragraph: Find $$\frac{\partial w}{\partial s}$$ if $$w = 4x + y^{2} + z^{3},x = e^{rs^{2}},y = \ln \left( \frac{r + s}{t} \right),$$ and $$z = rst^{2}.$$
If $$w = \sin (xyz),x = 1 - 3t,y = e^{1 - t},$$ and $$z = 4t,$$ find $$\frac{\partial w}{\partial t}.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, use this information: A function $$f(x,y)$$ is said to be homogeneous of degree $$n$$ if $$f(tx,ty) = t^{n}f(x,y).$$ For all homogeneous functions of degree $$n,$$ the following equation is true: $$x\frac{\partial f}{\partial x} + y\frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = nf(x,y).$$ Show that the given function is homogeneous and verify that $$x\frac{\partial f}{\partial x} + y\frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = nf(x,y).$$

solution.paragraph: $$f(tx,ty)=t2x2+t2y2=t1f(x,y),f(tx,ty)=t2x2+t2y2=t1f(x,y),$$ $$\partial f\partial y=x12(x2+y2)-1/2\times 2x+y12(x2+y2)-1/2\times 2y=1f(x,y)\partial f\partial y=x12(x2+y2)-1/2\times 2x+y12(x2+y2)-1/2\times 2y=1f(x,y)$$

problem.paragraph: The volume of a right circular cylinder is given by $$V(x,y) = \pi x^{2}y,$$ where $$x$$ is the radius of the cylinder and y is the cylinder height. Suppose $$x$$ and $$y$$ are functions of $$t$$ given by $$x = \frac{1}{2}t$$ and $$y = \frac{1}{3}t$$ so that $$x \text{and} y$$ are both increasing with time. How fast is the volume increasing when $$x = 2$$ and $$y = \frac{4}{3}?$$

The pressure $$P$$ of a gas is related to the volume and temperature by the formula $$PV = kT,$$ where temperature is expressed in kelvins. Express the pressure of the gas as a function of both $$V$$ and $$T.$$ Find $$\frac{dP}{dt}$$ when $$k = 1,$$ $$\frac{dV}{dt} = 2$$ cm3/min, $$\frac{dT}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}$$ K/min, $$V = 20$$ cm3, and $$T = 20^\circ \text{F} .$$

The radius of a right circular cone is increasing at $$3$$ cm/min whereas the height of the cone is decreasing at $$2$$ cm/min. Find the rate of change of the volume of the cone when the radius is $$13$$ cm and the height is $$18$$ cm.

solution.paragraph: $$d V d t = 1066 \pi 3 cm 3 / min d V d t = 1066 \pi 3 cm 3 / min$$

problem.paragraph: The volume of a frustum of a cone is given by the formula $$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi z\left( {x^{2} + y^{2} + xy} \right),$$ where $$x$$ is the radius of the smaller circle, $$y$$ is the radius of the larger circle, and $$z$$ is the height of the frustum (see figure). Find the rate of change of the volume of this frustum when $$x = 10 \text{in} \text{.,} y = 12 \text{in.,} \text{and} z = 18 \text{in} .$$ if $$\frac{dz}{dt} = - 5,\frac{dx}{dt} = 1,\frac{dy}{dt} = 1$$ (all in/min).

A closed box is in the shape of a rectangular solid with dimensions $$x,y, \text{and} z.$$ (Dimensions are in inches.) Suppose each dimension is changing at the rate of $$0.5$$ in./min. Find the rate of change of the total surface area of the box when $$x = 2 \text{in} \text{.,} y = 3 \text{in.,} \text{and} z = 1 \text{in} .$$

solution.paragraph: $$d A d t = 12 in . 2 / min d A d t = 12 in . 2 / min$$

problem.paragraph: The total resistance in a circuit that has three individual resistances represented by $$x,y,$$ and $$z$$ is given by the formula $$R(x,y,z) = \frac{xyz}{yz + xz + xy}.$$ Suppose at a given time the $$x$$ resistance is $$100 \text{Ω} ,$$ the y resistance is $$200 \text{Ω} ,$$ and the $$z$$ resistance is $$300 \text{Ω} .$$ Also, suppose the $$x$$ resistance is changing at a rate of $$2 \text{Ω} /\min ,$$ the $$y$$ resistance is changing at the rate of $$1 \text{Ω} /\min ,$$ and the $$z$$ resistance has no change. Find the rate of change of the total resistance in this circuit at this time.

The temperature $$T$$ at a point $$(x,y)$$ is $$T(x,y)$$ and is measured using the Celsius scale. A fly crawls so that its position after $$t$$ seconds is given by $$x = \sqrt{1 + t}$$ and $$y = 2 + \frac{1}{3}t,$$ where $$x \text{and} y$$ are measured in centimeters. The temperature function satisfies $$T_{x}\left( {2,3} \right) = 4$$ and $$T_{y}\left( {2,3} \right) = 3.$$ How fast is the temperature increasing on the fly’s path after $$3$$ sec?

solution.paragraph: $$2 ^\circ C/sec 2 ^\circ C/sec$$

problem.paragraph: The $$x \text{and} y$$ components of a fluid moving in two dimensions are given by the following functions: $$u(x,y) = 2y$$ and $$v(x,y) = -2x;$$ $$x \geq 0;y \geq 0.$$ The speed of the fluid at the point $$(x,y)$$ is $$s(x,y) = \sqrt{u{(x,y)}^{2} + v{(x,y)}^{2}}.$$ Find $$\frac{\partial s}{\partial x}$$ and $$\frac{\partial s}{\partial y}$$ using the chain rule.
